channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Ukraine Says Its Blysk Laser Shot Down a Jet-Powered Russian Drone in a World First
item.description: Ukraine says its Blysk laser air defence system has shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran drone in combat, in what Kyiv describes as the first time a laser has destroyed a jet-powered drone.

item.title: Bellingham Plays Down Zidane Comparisons After Wondergoal Sparks Real Madrid Comeback
item.description: Jude Bellingham came off the bench to score a stunning volley that turned Real Madrid's Champions League tie against PSV Eindhoven, then waved away comparisons with Zinedine Zidane, the club great whose shirt number he wears.

item.title: SpaceX Wins FCC Approval to Deploy One Million Data-Center Satellites in Orbit
item.description: The United States has authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites that will work as data centres in orbit, the first approval of its kind in the country's history, as demand for artificial intelligence computing keeps surging.

item.title: Boehly-Led Group Agrees to Buy Lukoil's Overseas Assets in $10 Billion Share Swap
item.description: A consortium led by US billionaire Todd Boehly has agreed to buy the overseas energy assets of sanctioned Russian oil producer Lukoil, in a deal structured as a share swap that would give the US government a stake in the business.

item.title: At Least 30 Killed as Fuel Tanker Overturns and Catches Fire on Cairo Ring Road
item.description: A fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on Cairo's ring road on Wednesday, killing at least 30 people and injuring 15, Egypt's health ministry said.

item.title: Ukraine Says Five Russian Warplanes Hit in Strike on Savasleyka Airfield
item.description: Ukraine said on Wednesday it had damaged five Russian military aircraft in a strike on an airfield about 300 kilometres east of Moscow that houses jets capable of carrying hypersonic missiles.

item.title: Hera Images Reveal Huge Crater on Asteroid Struck in Planetary Defence Test
item.description: The first close-up images of the asteroid deliberately struck by a spacecraft in a planetary defence test show a crater almost as large as the asteroid itself, four years after the impact.

item.title: Colombian Forces Storm Cartagena Supermarket, Free 20 Hostages After 17-Hour Siege
item.description: Troops and police in Colombia stormed a supermarket in the Caribbean city of Cartagena before dawn on Wednesday, freeing the last 20 hostages and shooting dead one of the gunmen, bringing a 17-hour siege to an end.

item.title: North Korea Expels Swiss Envoy and Orders Pyongyang Office Shut in Sanctions Row
item.description: North Korea has ordered Switzerland's envoy in Pyongyang to leave within 48 hours and demanded the closure of the Swiss diplomatic office, weeks after it reopened, in a row over Swiss sanctions on a North Korean children's camp.

item.title: World Records Six Straight Days More Than 2C Above Preindustrial Levels, a First
item.description: The world has recorded six consecutive days with average temperatures more than 2 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, the first time such a stretch has ever been measured.

item.title: Pete Edochie, Nollywood's Commanding Voice, Dies at 79
item.description: Veteran Nigerian actor Pete Edochie has died at the age of 79 after a long illness, his family has announced, closing a career that made him one of Nollywood's most recognisable faces.

item.title: Court Throws Out Report That Could Have Impeached South Africa's Ramaphosa
item.description: South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a court battle to set aside the report that paved the way for possible impeachment proceedings against him, ending parliament's inquiry into his handling of a 2020 burglary at his private game farm.

item.title: Leaked Russian Records Put Soldier Death Toll in Ukraine at Nearly 500,000
item.description: At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, leaked records from Russia's state statistics agency show, in the fullest measure yet of the war's human cost for Moscow.

item.title: Russian Strikes Kill at Least Five and Cut Power Across Five Ukrainian Regions
item.description: Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy system left at least five people dead, wounded dozens more and cut power for consumers in five regions, local authorities said on Wednesday.

item.title: Nineteen Civilians Killed as Drones Hit Homes in Sudan's Blue Nile State
item.description: Drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods in Damazin, the capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, have killed 19 civilians, including six women, and wounded 20 others, a Sudanese rights group said on Wednesday.

item.title: Israeli Strike Kills Senior Hamas Security Official and His Family in Gaza City
item.description: An Israeli airstrike on an apartment in the Shati refugee camp in western Gaza City has killed a senior Hamas security official, his wife and their two daughters, officials and medics said.

item.title: Nine Dead and 17 Trapped as Flood Swamps Unauthorised Gold Mine in Indonesia
item.description: Nine miners have been found dead and 17 more are believed trapped after floodwater poured into an unauthorised gold mine in Indonesia, as rescuers work to drain a shaft about 100 metres deep.

item.title: Nasdaq Falls 4% as AI Sell-Off Hits Wall Street and Nvidia Drops Again
item.description: Wall Street's technology sell-off deepened on Wednesday as the Nasdaq fell about 4 percent and Nvidia lost nearly 9 percent, with stubborn inflation and new tariff proposals adding to the pressure on investors.

item.title: Six Killed as Small Plane Crashes Into Sea Off Mississippi Coast
item.description: Six people, including two boys aged eight and ten, have been found dead after the small plane they were travelling in crashed into the sea off the Mississippi coast, the US Coast Guard said.

item.title: Sarkozy and Wife Carla Bruni Ordered to Stand Trial Over Witness Tampering
item.description: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, have been ordered to stand trial over alleged witness tampering in the long-running case over funding for his 2007 election campaign.

item.title: Britain Warns Firms Supplying Ukraine of Russian Sabotage Threat
item.description: Britain has warned companies that supply Ukraine's armed forces that they face a growing threat of sabotage from Russia, in an unusually public alert from its defence ministry and domestic security service.

item.title: Bangladesh Lifts Garment Workers' Minimum Pay 36% After Weeks of Protests
item.description: Bangladesh has lifted the monthly minimum for garment workers by 36 percent, to 17,000 taka, ending weeks of protests that shut factories and disrupted production in the country's biggest export industry.

item.title: Firms Tied to Alice Huang Financed $270 Million in AI Servers in China, Records Show
item.description: Companies linked to Alice Huang, the businesswoman at the centre of the scandal that briefly cost Nvidia chief Jensen Huang his job, raised financing against hundreds of powerful AI servers in China, financial records show.

item.title: Australia and Solomon Islands Sign Sweeping Security Treaty in Shift Away From China
item.description: Australia and Solomon Islands have signed a sweeping treaty that names Canberra as the Pacific nation's primary security partner and rules out any foreign military base on its soil, in a deal widely seen as a setback for China's ambitions in the region.

item.title: Houthis Say They Hit Saudi Arabia's Largest Oil Refinery as Coalition Strikes Hodeidah Port
item.description: The Houthis said on Wednesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery at Ras Tanura and Riyadh's financial district, as the Saudi-led coalition struck the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah after ordering civilians to evacuate.

item.title: Asian Shares Slide Sharply as Doubts Over the AI Boom Return
item.description: Shares across Asia fell sharply on Wednesday as renewed doubts about the artificial intelligence boom hammered chipmakers, wiping out the relief rally that followed Jensen Huang's return to the top of Nvidia.

item.title: US Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners, With China Facing the Highest Rate
item.description: The United States has now published the per-country rates behind its proposed tariffs on 14 major trading partners, with China facing a 20 percent duty that would rise to 40 percent if a trade truce lapses, and no duties able to take effect before a public hearing on January 25.

item.title: Ábrego García Arrives in Spain, Ending Two-Year Deportation Battle
item.description: Kilmar Ábrego García has arrived in Madrid, ending a nearly two-year legal fight over his deportation that at one point reached the country's highest court.

item.title: CIA and National Intelligence Office Suffer Apparent Cyberattack on Unclassified System
item.description: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence have suffered an apparent cyberattack affecting unclassified information, in the latest breach to hit the United States government.

item.title: Eisenkot's Coalition Hunt Turns to Ultra-Orthodox Parties as Lieberman Reverses Course
item.description: Avigdor Lieberman said on Wednesday that a government backed by the ultra-Orthodox parties could be presented by the end of next week, reversing his long-held opposition to such an arrangement.
